findings.title: Long-form output trims off the end after concatenating padded chunks
findings.evidence: TextToSpeech.__call__ concatenates full vocoder waveforms while adding only predicted durations. sample_noisy_latent rounds each latent length up to a chunk boundary (helper.py:165-169), and _infer returns wav unchanged. example_onnx.py:113 then trims the concatenated waveform to the sum of predicted durations. Internal padding remains in the middle, so the final trim removes audio from later chunks. Node and browser helpers have the same concatenate/sum-duration structure (nodejs/helper.js:289-299; web/helper.js:287-297).
findings.impact: Multi-chunk long-form exports contain extra gaps at chunk boundaries and lose the final portion of the synthesized passage as accumulated padding grows. Single-chunk output is unaffected by this particular bug.
findings.recommendation: Trim each individual waveform to its actual/predicted sample count before concatenating; compute the combined duration from the final concatenated sample count. Preserve independently trimmed rows for batched outputs.
findings.validation: Confirmed orchestration using the real Python helper with _infer replaced by deterministic padded outputs: two chunks [1,1,1,0,0] and [2,2,2,0,0], each with duration 0.3 s at 10 Hz, export as [1,1,1,0,0,2], losing the last two nonzero samples. No real ONNX model was run; the test proves padding/concatenation/trim behavior.
findings.classification: Confirmed through the validation described below

findings.title: The Python example does not enforce its maximum chunk length
findings.evidence: An overlong sentence is assigned unchanged to current_chunk; there is no word/character fallback. ASCII-only sentence boundary detection also misses Japanese punctuation.
findings.impact: Unpunctuated long passages and Japanese paragraphs bypass the intended 300/120-character inference limits, undermining the long-form chunking contract. No claim of measured runtime cost is made.
findings.recommendation: Split overlong sentences at words then at bounded character positions when no whitespace is available; cover Japanese sentence punctuation. Apply the same behavior to the SDK helper.
findings.validation: Real helper.chunk_text('word '*400,max_len=300) returns [1999] as the chunk length; reproduced without loading any model.
findings.classification: Confirmed through the validation described below

architecture.runtime_flow: Each language example loads external model assets from assets/onnx and preset style JSONs, normalizes text, predicts duration, encodes text, generates denoising latents and vocodes audio. Long-form helpers split text and concatenate chunk waveforms; CLI/UI code then exports WAV using the reported duration.

Equivalent local/browser runtime helpers and export/UI; source shows the same full-waveform concatenation versus summed-duration pattern.

contracts_to_preserve: Existing language-specific CLI flags, model/style input formats and CPU default.
Single-speaker output and batch row ordering; a single flattened batch array must not mix speaker samples.
Silence is inserted between chunks only, at the requested sample count.
Reported duration must agree with actual exported sample count within rounding tolerance.
The examples repository is independent of the supertonic-py package; SDK test counts are not evidence of example correctness.

change_surface: nodejs/helper.js: call and nodejs/example_onnx.js export parity
Native/mobile helpers only after source-specific confirmation
repair_steps: Add the recorded two-padded-chunk fixture as a regression using the real helper and deterministic _infer outputs. Include explicit nonzero markers in the final chunk so truncation is observable without playback.
Before concatenation, trim each waveform row to its own predicted/accepted sample count, clamped to actual available samples and using one explicit rounding rule.
Insert exactly the requested silence sample count between chunks. Sum actual sample counts after trimming/concatenation and derive the returned duration from that total.
Keep the batch path independently aware of each row's duration and padded row stride; do not flatten multiple speakers into one untrimmed long-form stream.
Check exporters for a redundant final trim and ensure it cannot remove another chunk's real samples because of floating-point rounding.

Port the accepted sample-count contract to Node/browser helpers that show the same pattern, and audit each native port independently. Add runtime-specific tests rather than claiming Python fixtures validate all ports.
invariants: Every intended non-padding sample from every chunk is emitted in order.
No vocoder padding is retained between chunks as unintended silence.
A final export trim does not cut later audio to compensate for earlier padding.
Returned duration matches the output sample count divided by sample_rate within one sample.
Batch row/speaker ordering and single-chunk output remain correct.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded fake chunks export as [1,1,1,2,2,2] at zero added silence, not [1,1,1,0,0,2].
With nonzero silence, output contains exactly the configured zero samples between complete chunks.
Different padding amounts across 3+ chunks do not change the final nonzero ending.
Duration/sample count agrees for odd sample counts and fractional predicted durations.
Real long-form speech retains the final word and expected pauses; this acoustic check remains NOT RUN.
regression_scenarios: Two and many chunks with different pad lengths
Predicted length exceeds available waveform; clamp or explicit error policy
English, Japanese/Korean chunk sizes and empty text behavior
risks: Trimming on predicted duration may expose off-by-one errors; use a single sample-count rule and clamp explicitly.
Duration predictions can differ from acoustically useful waveform tails; real speech listening must validate the chosen trim policy.
More than one platform repeats this algorithm; a Python-only repair does not establish native/browser parity.
findings.rollback: Retain pre-change generated output for comparison and revert only the concatenation/export correction if it corrupts sample ordering. Until repaired, synthesize/trim separate chunks outside the helper. No persisted schema migration is required.

findings.title: The Python example does not enforce its maximum chunk length
findings.evidence: An overlong sentence is assigned unchanged to current_chunk; there is no word/character fallback. ASCII-only sentence boundary detection also misses Japanese punctuation.
findings.impact: Unpunctuated long passages and Japanese paragraphs bypass the intended 300/120-character inference limits, undermining the long-form chunking contract. No claim of measured runtime cost is made.
findings.recommendation: Split overlong sentences at words then at bounded character positions when no whitespace is available; cover Japanese sentence punctuation. Apply the same behavior to the SDK helper.
findings.validation: Real helper.chunk_text('word '*400,max_len=300) returns [1999] as the chunk length; reproduced without loading any model.
change_surface: Model-free Python helper regression harness under a test location chosen by the maintainer
Other language helper chunkers only after auditing their own behavior
repair_steps: Define maximum length over Python Unicode characters and preserve the existing paragraph/sentence ordering and abbreviation rules.
For a sentence longer than max_len, split at available whitespace boundaries; if an individual span still exceeds the limit, split it by bounded character positions.
Recognize common Unicode sentence punctuation so Japanese text can retain useful boundaries; hard fallback must still enforce the maximum when punctuation/whitespace is absent.
Return nonempty bounded chunks without dropping, reordering or duplicating input text. Preserve the documented whitespace-normalization behavior.

Add regressions for unpunctuated words, one long word, Japanese text without spaces, Korean text, abbreviations and exact limits. Coordinate behavior with the sibling Python implementation without introducing a cross-repository runtime dependency.
invariants: Every returned chunk is nonempty and has len(chunk) <= configured max_len.
Original meaningful characters retain order and are emitted exactly once.
Empty/whitespace input and existing sentence/paragraph behavior remain defined.
Minimum-limit validation remains consistent with the public SDK or example contract.
acceptance_criteria: chunk_text('word '*400,max_len=300) returns multiple chunks, all <=300, instead of [1999].
A Japanese passage longer than 120 characters with no ASCII whitespace yields bounded chunks while preserving all characters.
One token longer than the limit is split safely and recombines to the original token.
Existing abbreviation and paragraph tests remain green.
regression_scenarios: One very long word and one long sentence
Emoji, combining marks and expression-tag text
Empty input, repeated whitespace, paragraphs and common abbreviations
risks: A strict character fallback may split a grapheme cluster or expression tag, affecting synthesis quality. Prefer safe text boundaries while maintaining a real length bound; define behavior for indivisible tokens explicitly.
More chunks add pauses and inference overhead. Exact memory/latency improvements and audio quality have not been measured.
findings.rollback: Revert the chunker change if it drops text or materially degrades speech; clients can pre-split bounded passages temporarily. No data format migration is required.
